rationale: Positive/negative PMD fixtures exercise the actual custom rules and wiring; explicit cases are more useful than a generic fixture framework.
SpotBugs matching fixtures protect exact suppression scope; legacy class-name strings are test inputs, not runtime Mesos dependencies.
Shutdown executes callbacks while holding the waiter monitor and consumes interrupts; model shutdown completion and callback ownership explicitly.
LIFO/idempotent cleanup is useful, but executing arbitrary actions under the registry monitor needs a deliberate snapshot-and-completion design.
Shutdown qualifier is a small, meaningful Guice binding boundary.
Command is tiny; replacing it alone would churn shutdown bindings without simplifying ownership.
The no-op command constant is already explicit and shared.
Consumer composition preserves ordering and short-circuit failure; migrate its Guava predicate seam only with StateMachine callers.
Checked-exception-preserving command has semantics Runnable cannot express.
Checked-exception supplier remains useful in retry code; avoid wrapping exceptions to remove one interface.
String validation already uses isBlank and preserves returned identity and exception formatting.
Replace the exhaustion LoadingCache with simple iterator state and enforce next-after-exhaustion semantics.
Pair supports nulls and deep array equality; mechanical record replacement would change method-signature matching.
Private-module exposure and qualifier checks express real injection constraints; overloaded generic KeyFactory is not a lambda seam.
Per-method SlidingStats registration/cache and Guice interception are meaningful; finalizing intercepted classes would be unsafe.
Use bracket-aware address parsing/formatting while preserving wildcard and unresolved-host behavior.
Small explicit abort endpoint; its authorization belongs to HTTP policy, not a syntax rewrite.
Independent thread snapshots can contain terminated or absent entries; use coherent/null-tolerant diagnostics and label platform-thread scope.
Health supplier and legacy OK/SICK response contract are simple; no local abstraction change needed.
The per-request shutdown thread should delegate to the owned, idempotent shutdown coordinator while preserving asynchronous response behavior.
Use current thread IDs and state the platform-only dump scope; getAllStackTraces does not describe virtual-thread activity.
Consume one detached series snapshot; ResponseStruct is a narrow record candidate with names/data JSON and zero-fill contracts preserved.
Keep sorted text output while filtering export inputs and replacing the transform/list/sort/join chain locally if useful.
Keep ordered numeric JSON/pretty formatting; apply safe export policy and reuse configured immutable Gson instances.
Mixed-unit equality disagrees with hashCode and integral conversions go through double; narrow time values toward Duration with characterized numeric boundaries.
Keep byte-unit spelling and factors at configuration boundaries while exact internal quantity types replace generic Amount incrementally.
Time units and CLI display remain compatibility adapters during an incremental Duration migration.
The unit contract need not change independently of the numeric representation; avoid generic-signature churn.
Unrestricted environment/property/argument export needs an allowlist; modernize MXBean usage and label platform-thread metrics.
Bounded sampled percentile windows and ordered first-percentile sampling are real semantics; do not parallelize or stream them blindly.
A named timestamp/value sample record would clarify the Pair-based window; preserve Ticker, window direction and counter sampling semantics.
NaN/zero fallback and infinity behavior are explicit and tested; keep the straightforward implementation.
RecordingStat distinguishes active sampling from reading the last value; useful interface boundary.
Wrapper normalizes names and adapts ordinary stats to sampling; a record adds little here.
Request counters, percentile sampling and shared rate registration are cohesive; preserve registration order.
Volatile cached sample with final sample method is a meaningful concurrency contract.
Timeable variants preserve checked exceptions and no-result actions; timer finally block correctly records failed actions too.
Named readable statistic is a minimal useful interface.
Named-stat base shares validation; no forced record conversion of extensible subclasses.
Registry interface isolates ordered sampling from global implementation.
Three static registries and inconsistent collision/retention policies need a scoped registry design, preserving derived-stat order.
Injected metrics capability is worth keeping as the seam for registry ownership; collection-size default is already small.
Iterable sample views need an explicit detached snapshot contract rather than apparent read-only live data.
Expose an atomic multi-series snapshot so callers cannot mix timestamp/sample generations.
Unmodifiable views escape the sampler lock; seconds conversion also loses subsecond periods and the name cache is permanent.
Keep LIFO teardown but preserve original cleanup failures with suppression and clear actions even when teardown fails.
Pattern matching or the existing TypeToken API can remove manual type casts; preserve nested-generic mocking and unsupported-type diagnostics.
Retry helper exposes checked errors and deterministic wait injection; not improved by CompletableFuture layering.
Backoff continuation/calculation interface makes retry policy testable without sleeping.
Classloader resource stream is not closed; use try-with-resources and a detached property snapshot.
Wall time, monotonic time and waiting are distinct test seams; java.time.Clock alone is not a drop-in replacement.
Small deterministic random seam supports sampler/backoff tests; RandomGenerator migration is optional and coordinated.
Threshold sampler has direct validation and behavior; no additional policy object needed.
Capture from-state under the transition lock and freeze builder rules; retain outside-lock/reentrant callback semantics deliberately.
Backoff conversion is another Amount boundary; retain jitter behavior while making conversion precision and overflow explicit.
StringTemplate integration is a contained compatibility seam; keep bean getters used by template reflection.
Small predictable build-info fake; collection factory churn has little value.
FakeClock explicitly combines test wall/monotonic time; preserve controllable time until time interfaces migrate together.
Manual Guava Ticker is useful for cache expiry and rate tests; do not replace with wall-clock time.
Content equality with array-identity hash and exposed mutable bytes break value semantics; use defensive copies and array-aware hashing.
Leadership/control callback protocol is still used by lifecycle and discovery; avoid removing it merely because HA work is deferred.
ACL constants and path normalization serve the legacy discovery compatibility boundary.
Embedded ZooKeeper ownership is explicit through teardown; retained for actual discovery integration tests.
Test server supports network restart and session expiration; retain this intentional test seam until the ZooKeeper dependency migration.
Tests protect consumer order and exception short-circuiting; keep during any functional-interface migration.
Exception-format tests catch without fail-on-no-throw; assertThrows would make those checks meaningful.
Add explicit exhaustion and remove-state cases; existing zip-longest/default/removal cases remain valuable.
Null-slot and extractor tests preserve Pair compatibility; array behavior needs protection if a future caller-specific replacement occurs.
Covers Jakarta qualifiers and private binding exposure; trivial constructor cleanup is not a roadmap item.
Existing wildcard/IPv4/unresolved tests should be extended with bracketed IPv6 and no-reverse-DNS formatting.
Small shared stat-supplier fixture keeps endpoint tests focused on serialization.
Keep JSON column order and time filtering; add snapshot stability during concurrent sampling when repository API changes.
Retain exact sorted text expectations and add safe-export boundary coverage using synthetic secrets.
Keep exact numeric and pretty JSON fixtures when caching codecs and filtering unsafe stats.
Current mixed-unit equality tests omit hash collections and large exact integer conversions.
Flush helper iterates empty varargs and checks the field instead of its parameter; reverse-input test also supplies ascending data.
Deterministic Ticker tests cover windows, negative rates and rate-of-rate order; preserve them around sample-record cleanup.
Recent NaN, signed zero and infinity regression cases capture intentional behavior.
Tests distinguish timing success and exceptions; retain checked/no-result interface coverage.
Explicitly tests duplicate counter instances being unregistered; registry collision changes must deliberately revise this contract.
Only sequential ordering/backfill is tested; add detached snapshots, eviction overlap and subsecond sampling coverage.
Nested generic mock fixture justifies retaining the TypeToken-based helper boundary.
Tests checked exception transparency and retry stopping with an injected clock; no reason to add real sleeps.
Deterministic threshold test avoids probabilistic assertions and is already concise.
Current transition cases are sequential; add concurrent from-state and post-build rule mutation tests before state-machine cleanup.
Backoff tests cover ordinary bounds; add conversion edge cases only when migrating Amount/time representations.
Template fixture intentionally has bean getters and exact whitespace output; records would need compatibility verification.
FakeClockTest actually exercises FakeTicker; rename it and add true FakeClock tests without wall-clock sleeps.
Pure path normalization test unnecessarily starts embedded ZooKeeper via its base class; use a plain test.
BenchmarkSettings is an immutable data carrier suited to a record; preserve builder defaults and collection ownership.
Rack index increments after the first host, producing a one-host first rack; derive rack from i/hostsPerRack.
Update fixtures deliberately create event-heavy snapshots; simple loops express fixture shape clearly.
IntStream.range(1, ports) produces ports-minus-one entries; clarify the intended cardinality before benchmark comparison.
Trial-lived scheduling state eventually changes workload and no-op futures violate executor contracts; keep synchronous isolation but bound/reset workload.
Snapshot benchmark constructs a lazy operation stream without consuming it; it currently does not measure restoration work.
Insertion benchmark accumulates tasks across invocations until trial teardown; define and reset state for comparable results.
Status benchmark grows retained tasks and starts/stops without awaiting lifecycle; bound fixtures and waits before using throughput claims.
Current task-store benchmark selects MemStorage; add explicit SQLite cases for production optimization decisions.
Static non-atomic task IDs and mutable fixtures need explicit single-thread assumptions or deterministic scoped ID ownership.
Read-only API fixtures measure memory storage; identify backend and fixture-size scope in modern performance qualification.
Update-store measurements use memory storage and fetch full details in both variants; name/parameterize the actual measured operation.
Capability fake already uses a Launch record; no protocol implementation belongs in this benchmark stub.
Explicit no-op event sink keeps benchmark effects isolated.
getAll returns null where other no-op queries return empty; return an empty collection or explicitly reject unexpected use.
Zero rescheduling fake clearly isolates measured state-management work.
No-op benchmark stats intentionally differ from recording test stats; merging them would change benchmark overhead.
Use pinned Guava's built-in immutable collectors, auditing UNORDERED/iteration behavior; service-manager adapter remains a useful test seam.
Replace Pair<String,Class<?>[]> with a named signature value using List<Class<?>>; preserve overload and inherited-method matching.
Deflater ownership and reflective constructor handling were already modernized and byte-compatibility tested; keep those safeguards.
Application-start qualifier expresses lifecycle grouping with little code.
Future completion and retry scheduling occur before commit; correct outcome ownership first, then simplify WorkItem/Result representations.
Constructor-owned callbacks, timers and reentrant shutdown span state and resource lifetimes; extract named actions under one explicit shutdown order.
Own the privately created lifecycle executor instead of relying on VM exit; keep batch service bindings and sizes.
Startup and leader-active ServiceManager groups represent real readiness boundaries; avoid replacing lifecycle services with a generic executor.
UUID identity no longer requires a clock binding; preserve format, sanitization and uniqueness.
Small typed status ingress hides transport details appropriately.
Status acknowledgements correctly follow the entire write; preserve that boundary and do not merge blindly with BatchWorker.
Read host attributes once per task event; separate bounded status counters from unbounded job/rack/role metric names.
TierInfo is a narrow record candidate retaining isPreemptible/isRevocable/isProduction and exact JSON property names.
TierConfig can be immutable named data with defensive map copying; retain default-tier validation and external default property name.
One-time startup parsing is already contained; mapper caching has negligible benefit here compared with request-path codecs.
RegisterGauges owns an executor reference but performs no shutdown; make async work lifetime explicit without interrupting active transactions.
afterExecute handles failures and interruption but lets CancellationException escape; handle normal cancellation and define scheduled-task cleanup policy.
Instance key validation and canonical formatting are direct; preserve nonnegative ID checks.
Job key helpers preserve strict identifier and three-component parsing semantics; standard split replacement needs trailing-empty care.
Arrow cases simplify status classification; expose immutable state-set views rather than mutable public EnumSet constants.
Guava range/domain operations encode inclusive integer ranges and compact views; loops are clearer than nested stream replacements.
Query.Builder is persistent copy-on-write over Thrift; document semantics and keep empty/unset distinctions before any record/domain-query redesign.
Domain exception constructors are standard and sufficient.
TaskGroupKey can be a small record with compatibility accessor and custom job-name toString; retain nonnull canonical task.
Make public state sets immutable and use modern last-element/comparator idioms without changing explicit status precedence.
Precompiled identifier regex, null and length validation already express the contract clearly.
Typed event publication capability is useful independently of EventBus implementation.
Decorator keeps veto notification apart from placement policy; retain interception and result identity.
Selected immutable events can be records, but task sets need copies and webhook JSON must remain explicitly serialized rather than reflecting record layout.
Own registration executor and subscriber unregistration; keep synchronous fail-closed recovery and separate asynchronous registration semantics.
Constructor logs credential-bearing config and module-created client lifetime needs partial-start ownership; preserve delivery/metric behavior.
Redact header values and sensitive URI components in toString; keep Jackson names and null-versus-wildcard status semantics during any value cleanup.
HTTP client is allocated during Guice configure before its service starts; move acquisition into an owned lifecycle/provider with failure cleanup.
Periodic service wrappers and revocable-resource adapter encode separate schedules and resource semantics; no generic scheduler framework needed.
Cache enforces single metric registration; replace only as part of registry/cardinality ownership, not as an isolated computeIfAbsent fashion change.
Aggregation-local LoadingCache is unnecessary; use a local map and computeIfAbsent, preserving mutable accumulation before returning results.
Compute minima without intermediate sets and group resource slots once; preserve missing-vector behavior and zero-valued groups.
Metric registry and sampling config bindings are the migration seam for snapshot and registry ownership changes.
Five independent active-task scans and two quota reads can become one coherent aggregate snapshot; reset disappeared per-role metrics explicitly.
Recording stats fake is intentionally lightweight and single-owner; do not conflate it with benchmark no-op stats.
Collector tests should characterize duplicate keys, encounter order and parallel collection before dropping custom collectors.
Preserve inherited/overload/whitelist interception tests and add array-parameter signature matching for a named signature value.
Existing failure listener test checks only synchronous happy cleanup; cover reentrant/failing shutdown alongside coordinator changes.
Historical compressed bytes and failure-cause tests protect recent codec modernization; do not replace exact fixture assertions with mere round trips.
Tests explicitly preserve pre-commit success and poll-to-tail ordering; revise only with a deliberate transaction-outcome contract and real SQLite rollback cases.
Offer CPU/memory/revocable cases protect placement resource interpretation; concise table-driven style is already used.
Lifecycle tests cover ordering with mocks; add partial startup failure, concurrent defeat/registration and bounded timer cleanup.
Covers sanitized ID prefix and distinct valid UUIDs without the removed clock dependency.
Batch acknowledgement tests explicitly verify post-commit and all-or-nothing behavior; retain as contrast for BatchWorker correction.
Retain startup replay/lost-counter semantics and add one host-attribute read plus registry/cardinality retirement coverage.
Tier value refactor must keep default, mismatch and production-flag compatibility cases.
Retain strict unknown-property rejection and default JSON names when TierConfig becomes a value record.
Test starts services but never stops them; add owned teardown with executor lifecycle changes.
Executors are left alive and normal cancellation lacks coverage; use deterministic cancellation/termination assertions.
All-status classification test protects arrow-switch conversion and immutable status-set work.
Range grouping examples protect inclusive boundaries; do not rewrite compact range abstraction to materialized integer lists.
Rich legacy task fixture remains useful for wire compatibility; add explicit Go-profile fixtures rather than silently changing all defaults.
Keep custom status-precedence/latest-event assertions when simplifying comparator helpers and state constants.
Decorator tests correctly distinguish veto/no-veto notification and forwarded result.
Keep synchronous recovery/fail-closed tests while adding actual registration-executor termination coverage.
Exact oldState Optional-shape JSON fixtures must survive event/value-record changes; do not derive wire output from record layout.
Close per-test HTTP clients, remove shared mutable builders and use controlled local failures; update toString assertions to protect redaction.
Revocable/nonrevocable offer adapter expectations protect intentionally shared noncompressible resources.
Preserve quota, role and dedicated/nonproduction aggregates while introducing one-pass snapshots; add disappearing-role reset checks.
Existing missing-vector, tiny-slot and explicit record-hash tests constrain allocation cleanup; add zero-reset checks where needed.
Use real completedFuture instead of mocking a CompletableFuture's get method; callers should observe actual completion behavior.
Fake scheduler returns null futures and models no cancellation; add a cancellable scheduled handle before relying on it for shutdown qualification.
